title: Remove duplicates from Sorted array
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Remove duplicates in-place from a sorted array; return the new length.
intuition: Because the array is sorted, duplicates are adjacent. A write pointer marks the boundary of the unique prefix while a read pointer scans ahead.

approaches.title: Brute: set then rewrite
approaches.idea: Insert into a set, sort it back into the array.
limitations: Ignores the sorted precondition; extra O(n) memory

approaches.title: Optimal: two pointers, in-place
approaches.idea: i marks the last unique slot; j scans; copy only when a[j] != a[i].
approaches.whyWorks: Invariant: a[0..i] is the deduplicated version of a[0..j].

commonMistakes: Assuming the tail of the array is cleared
patternRecognition: In-place compaction -> slow write pointer + fast read pointer
followUps: Allow each value at most twice
